art:map-atlas.title: The Atlas World — Mariners' Chart
art:map-atlas.note: AUTHORED VECTOR, NOT GENERATED. Drawn by tools/mapforge/render-sheet.mjs --sheet atlas from content/spine/ (the redrawn 36-node trunk + sheet-atlas.json); the SVG beside this PNG (maps/atlas-world.svg) is the artifact, the PNG beside it is a 512px review thumb of it for the storybook card. It does NOT draw the west coast line or the Meltwash river — STATE §28 ruling 8 retired both from this sheet; Task 8 re-draws that ground on its own continent sheet, which does not exist yet.
art:map-atlas.description: The world sheet on the redrawn 400×400 km frame of n-atlas, drawn from one seed: thirteen landmasses, three ocean polygons with nine marginal seas nested inside them, 47 settlement marks — one per f-town-* feature, three of them harbours because a sea lane ends there — and the two sea lanes lettered at the ports they leave from. Only REPORTED ground is filled, which is four of the thirteen: two ice caps take the ice pattern and two take the frontier hatch, while the nine surveyed landmasses draw as outline with their regions and towns on them, and the two surveyed region bounds are the only ones lettered. Honest empty parchment everywhere the survey has never reached. Thirty-two names asked, thirty-two placed, none dropped, against a thirty-two-label budget the sheet now sits exactly on. No scale bar; the hand note says why.

art:map-synthetic-density.title: Target-Density Canary — not geography
art:map-synthetic-density.note: TEST INSTRUMENT, NOT SHIPPED ART. No player ever sees this sheet: it is drawn by tools/mapforge/lib/synthetic-sheet.mjs from a committed parameter fixture, at the size of the world Plan C generates, so a render regression at target density is visible against today's small chart. It is manifested because scripts/check_asset_manifest.mjs FAILS on any file under game-client/assets/art/ with no entry — the earlier plan to leave it out was checked against the gate and does not survive it.
art:map-synthetic-density.description: A synthetic chart at the agreed target density — 13 landmasses, 160 regions, 1,740 landform glyph instances at the 18 px family-identity minimum, and 340 decluttered labels — on the atlas sheet's own 400 km, 1400 x 1400 px frame, over a baked biome-texture underlay with the full 25-row legend beneath it. Every ring, mark and name is generated from one integer hash; none of it is a place.

art:town-millcross.title: Millcross — the crossing
art:town-millcross.note: Z-Image Turbo, local generation, ABP_1 from A1-geography-cluster1.md art briefs — PLACEHOLDER: below the §6.0 asset quality bar (turbo model, single pass, no upscaler); regenerate when an environment-capable model is installed.
art:town-millcross.description: Millcross, a sprawling wall-less crossing town on both banks of a grey river, seen from the road at cart height in late afternoon. One mill-wheel housing is the only structure above one storey; a queue of loaded carts and led animals stretches toward the ford, and former refugee tents have grown plank walls with real doorframes.

art:town-embervale.note: Z-Image Turbo, local generation, ABP_1 from A1-geography-cluster1.md art briefs — PLACEHOLDER: below the §6.0 asset quality bar (turbo model, single pass, no upscaler); regenerate when an environment-capable model is installed.
art:town-embervale.description: Embervale, a terraced hill town of six stacked ledges seen from the fields below at dusk, each ledge a row of slate roofs above a black clinker retaining wall. Forty low hearth-smoke plumes stand off the roofs, and ember-red banners hang along every ledge above figures in banded mourning cloth over faded militia colours.

art:town-gildmark.description: Gildmark, a vertical port town stacked in five terraces up a rock headland, seen from the water at the end of the coastal road in low sun. Dressed stone at the base gives way to rendered plaster and timber above, every seaward face tarred black against the salt, with a glazed-cap tower crowning the silhouette above mudflats studded with wrecked-hull ribs.

art:town-rooktide.description: Rooktide, a low river town on stepped terraces above a tidal landing at slack low water, its barges sitting in mud on their pilings while thousands of rooks work the exposed flats. Long shallow-roofed sheds step up the bank, every building visibly sewn from old salvaged plank into newer timber, with barge cranes dominating the foreground.

art:town-cindervast.description: Cindervast, a roofless walled city on an upland rock shoulder seen from a day's walk below at dusk. art:map-fabric.title: The Generated World — Fabric Survey
art:map-fabric.note: AUTHORED VECTOR, NOT GENERATED ART. Drawn by tools/mapforge/render-sheet.mjs --sheet fabric from content/world/fabric/ and from nothing else — deliberately NOT from the spine, so a reviewer can see what the fabric says on its own. Before the redraw that mattered because the committed trunk said something else entirely; now the trunk is promoted from this same fabric, and the independence is what makes any disagreement between the two visible at all. The SVG beside this PNG (maps/world-fabric.svg) is the artifact; the PNG is a 512px review thumb of it for the storybook card.
art:map-fabric.description: The generated world as the fabric layer records it: 13 landmasses traced from their own coastlines (outerRing, 2,431 vertices over the thirteen — not the trunk placement rings, which the vertex cap tightens to as few as 12), 160 regions drawn as divisions of land with the 40 surveyed ones inked and firmly outlined against the 120 reported ones left as bare parchment under a faint line, 47 settlement dots sized by rank (3 capitals, 12 hubs, 32 villages), 40 roads dashed, 7 trunk rivers, and the two sea lanes joining the three capitals in bell-bronze. No biome fills, no glyphs, no place names — naming is Plan D's and rich cartography is Plan B's, so the continent ids stand in as labels and the emptiness is honest.

art:map-overlay.title: Coastline Overlay — Baseline vs Generated
art:map-overlay.note: AUTHORED VECTOR, NOT GENERATED ART. Drawn by tools/mapforge/render-sheet.mjs --sheet overlay. The baseline is read from the draft folder's baseline/ copy when one is present and from content/spine/nodes otherwise — NEVER from git, so the sheet builds in a dirty worktree and in a container with no repository. The SVG beside this PNG is the artifact; the PNG is a 512px review thumb.
art:map-overlay.description: The baseline trunk's continent polygons ghosted at 20% opacity under the generated coastlines at full ink, with the 160 region divisions faint behind them, and a per-continent area-delta table joined through content/world/manifest.json's landmasses[].nodeId. Since the redraw the committed trunk IS drawn from this fabric, so the sheet no longer shows a before/after: it reads 13 baseline polygons against 13 generated, nothing marked NEW, per-continent factors between x0.99 and x1.05, and a total of 65,498.4 -> 65,599.5 km² of gross land at x1.00, with sea:land 1.44 : 1 on the committed trunk, the figure G-SEALAND measures; the sheet's own footer line quotes the fabric layer's generated figure instead, and the two are different measures of the same world. What it measures now is the trunk against the fabric it was drawn from — a drift check, not a comparison of two worlds.
